ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Florence Nightingale Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for nearly three years of exhausting fatigue that worsens after exertion. Concerns: Nearly three years of exhausting fatigue since a severe febrile illness on an overseas deployment, with crashes lasting days after any push of work; Lightheaded with a racing heart when standing in a line or at the stove; Wants above all to keep doing her statistical and policy work, even if much of it has to be done from her sofa or bed. [S]

tr.td: Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, one to two tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for muscle pain or headache, no more than 3 g a day
One to two tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed; no more than 3 g a day
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 50 mcg (2,000 units) oral tablet, one tablet by mouth daily

Ten-minute passive standing test (NASA lean test): heart rate 66/min supine and 92/min at 10 minutes (rise of 26/min); blood pressure 106/68 supine and 102/70 standing; lightheadedness and leg mottling from minute 6; no orthostatic hypotension and below the 30/min threshold for postural tachycardia syndrome
Repeat ten-minute passive standing test: heart rate 68/min supine and 86/min at 10 minutes (rise of 18/min); blood pressure 108/70 supine and 106/72 standing; mild lightheadedness only after minute 8
Hepatitis B vaccine, adult three-dose series completed

tr.td: Crimean fever at Balaclava: dangerously ill and near death, then a slow and painful recovery; she called it typhus
Retrospective interpretation of the Crimean fever as brucellosis, without laboratory confirmation (possible, not established)

Overwork and failing health during the army health commission, with rest at Malvern, a collapse with cardiac symptoms, then nausea, insomnia, and palpitations; took to her bed or couch on doctors' orders but kept working

Two-week review of exclusion tests, ME/CFS diagnosis and care plan, and infectious diseases consultation
Same-day sick visit for a cold with an ME/CFS flare

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnose ME/CFS by clinical criteria after exclusion tests, explain that it is a real illness with no diagnostic test, and give her a written care and support plan, including a flare plan

Energy management led by the patient: an activity and symptom diary, planned rest before and between tasks, work broken into short blocks, and heart-rate awareness; no graded exercise therapy or fixed increases in activity
Infectious diseases consultation to look for relapsed or focal brucellosis or another persisting infection before attributing her symptoms to ME/CFS
Orthostatic intolerance measures: 2 to 2.5 L of fluid a day, more salt with meals, waist-high compression garments, and tasks done seated or reclined; repeat the standing test at six months
Sleep, pain, and cognitive symptom care: a regular sleep window with rest periods kept short, acetaminophen as needed, no sedatives or opioids, and memory aids for work
Vitamin D repletion with cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily, rechecked after about three months
Review the care plan at every visit, with PHQ-9, PROMIS fatigue and physical function scores, and a pain score; primary care review at least yearly and more often while the plan is new
Workplace adjustments: home working, a reclined workstation, flexible hours, and meetings by video or at her home
Agree an energy management plan with a stable baseline and no more than one crash a month by the six-month review
One flare in three months, after a cold; no crash from overexertion since the summer
Keep working within her energy limits, aiming for four hours a day in planned blocks by the six-month review
Working four to five hours a day in 45-minute blocks with rest between
Fewer orthostatic symptoms with fluids, salt, compression, and seated or reclined tasks by the three-month review
Lightheaded on standing two or three times a week instead of daily
Replete vitamin D to 30 ng/mL or higher

list.item: Moderate ME/CFS at intake: independent in self-care but housebound most days, walks about 10 minutes before symptoms worsen, and needs a rest after showering; works about three hours a day, reclined, in short blocks [S]
By the six-month review: fewer crashes, out of the house twice a week, and working four to five hours a day in planned blocks with rest between [S]
Alert, precise, and articulate; tires visibly toward the end of a long conversation and loses words at times [S]
Mood frustrated by her limits but not depressed; no hopelessness; PHQ-9 score 8 drawn mainly from the fatigue, sleep, and concentration items, with item 9 scored 0 [S]
